Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal pulled the Order Form and flagged the Security Exhibit language for SOC 2 and penetration testing: they want clearer notice timing for pen tests, evidence cadence for SOC 2 artifacts, and stronger alignment on sampled assertions.

High level asks from Acme Legal:
- 30-day notice for pen tests where feasible (they understand emergency tests may be different)
- Evidence cadence: weekly snapshots for 90 days around major releases; monthly otherwise
- Clarify which SOC 2 assertions Redwood will map to shared artifacts (esp. CC6 and CC7 related controls)

Can you share a redline of the Security Exhibit + a proposed pen-test window and responsible owners for evidence? We need this for our procurement review (legal + infosec).

Attaching the ordering doc we have on our side (stub).

Appreciate it —

Thanks Erin — we can absolutely tighten this up. Looping in Laura (assurance) and Karthik (legal) to propose language and an ops plan.

Quick responses to your bullets:
- Pen-test notice: Redwood typically requests 10 business days for standard scheduled assessments; we can scope an alternate 30-day notice for enterprise Order Forms if it aligns with capacity planning. We should capture what "emergency" means (e.g., active incident vs. proactive testing).
- Evidence cadence: the weekly snapshot for 90-day windows is doable for major releases; need to confirm which artifacts Acme needs (audit logs, config snapshots, SOC 2 control map).
- SOC 2 assertions: we will map our artifact buckets to the assertions you called out — I'll ask Laura to attach the control mapping and sample artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik to propose redline language for the Security Exhibit and Order Form carve-outs (legal).
2) Laura to propose a concrete evidence cadence and a 30/10 policy option for pen-test notice (assurance).
3) I will schedule a 30-minute alignment call with Acme infosec + legal next week.

When is Tom available? Erin — if you share two slots, we’ll lock one.

— David

Head of Customer Security Partnerships

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: SOC2 assertions + pen-test ask (Order Form)

Thanks — I reviewed Acme's stub and sketched a targeted redline (attachment: orderform-diff.txt) with the following high-level positions so legal and product are aligned: 

1) Pen-test notice: propose a dual-path approach in the exhibit:
   - Standard tests: 10 business days' notice; Redwood will provide a staging endpoint and ephemeral creds where applicable.
   - Customer-requested extended-window: 30 calendar days' notice if customer requires longer planning; Redwood may apply a scheduling fee if it materially changes capacity planning.

2) Emergency tests: allow immediate triage-based testing by Acme only with prior written approval from Redwood Security (we propose a 24-hour incident notification and post-test blameless post-mortem).

3) Evidence cadence and scope: define artifact buckets rather than enumerating every log. Proposed buckets: SOC2 control map (mapping file), change-control snapshots, access logs (sampled), and configuration export for affected services. For the 90-day major-release window, limit to weekly snapshots of these buckets; outside of that window provide monthly snapshots for 6 months, then on-request thereafter.

4) Liability/assurance carveouts: any generated artifacts that include customer data should be delivered under mutual redaction rules; add a short clause on data minimization when providing artifacts.

I'll inline exact redline suggestions in the attached orderform-diff.txt. If product needs broader exceptions (e.g., staging gating), call them out and I will adjust.

— Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: orderform-diff.txt (plain text, 3 KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:40:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: SOC2 assertions + pen-test ask (Order Form)

Adding implementation details from Assurance/OPS and a proposed schedule (attachment: pen-test-scope.xlsx).

Operational proposal (concise):
- Pen-test windows: two options for Acme to pick in Order Form:
  Option A (standard): 10 business day notice + standard staging access + weekly snapshot only during the test week.
  Option B (enterprise): 30 calendar day advanced notice, dedicated coordination lane, weekly snapshots for 90 days around a major release (start/end dates to be mutually agreed).

- Responsible owners:
  - Evidence owner: Laura Bennett (Assurance) — will coordinate extraction and redaction.
  - Platform ops contact: Monica Patel — will own staging credentials and ephemeral host provisioning.
  - Legal liaison: Karthik Iyer — will finalize redline language and escalation path.

- Artifact examples: weekly snapshots will include:
  1) SOC 2 mapping (control -> artifact) in CSV
  2) Access log subset (time-windowed and redacted)
  3) Configuration snapshot (service-level, non-sensitive)
  4) Change-control export for impacted components
- Delivery: secure ShareFile link with 90-day retention by default; longer retention negotiable in Order Form.

We can support the weekly snapshot cadence for a 90-day period for enterprise Option B. Sample pen-test window: 2026-11-15 through 2026-11-22 (tentative) — subject to Acme confirmation and Redwood capacity planning.

Erin/Tom: does that sample window work for your schedule? If not, propose two alternatives and we'll swap.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Assurance
Redwood Inference
